title: Complete-intersection local rings are invariant under field extension
statement: Let $k\to K$ be an extension of fields, let $C$ be a finite type commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], put $C_K=K\otimes_k C$, and let $\mathfrak q_K$ be a prime ideal of $C_K$ with inverse image $\mathfrak q$ under $C\to C_K$, $c\mapsto1\otimes c$. Then $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$ if and only if $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Here a complete-intersection local ring over a field $F$ means a local $F$-algebra isomorphic to a quotient of a regular local $F$-algebra [def-weil-regular-scheme] essentially of finite type over $F$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] by an ideal generated by a finite regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. No separability or algebraicity assumption on $K/k$ is made.

source.place: Tag 00SI (lemma-lci-field-change-local), with the local-ring meaning of complete intersection in definition-lci-local-ring.

proof.text: Choose a finite presentation $P=k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $I$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-base-change], the scalar extension has the presentation $C_K\cong P_K/I_K$ with $P_K=K[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ and $I_K$ generated by the coefficientwise images of $I$. Thus both algebras are finite type over their respective fields, and the primes in the statement have inverse images $\mathfrak q'\subset P$ and $\mathfrak q_K'\subset P_K$.

source.place: Tag 00SI, proof lines 36215--36229 (choice of presentation and its scalar extension).

proof.text: The local dimensions agree: [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-field-extension] gives $d:=\dim_{\mathfrak q}(\operatorname{Spec}C)=\dim_{\mathfrak q_K}(\operatorname{Spec}C_K)$.

source.place: Tag 00SI, proof lines 36230--36233, invoking the dimension-under-field-extension lemma.

proof.text:
The new conormal-fibre comparison [lem-trf-lci-conormal-fibre-field-change] gives a canonical identification
$$ (I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{C_{\mathfrak q}}\kappa(\mathfrak q)\otimes_{\kappa(\mathfrak q)}\kappa(\mathfrak q_K)\cong (I_K/I_K^2)_{\mathfrak q_K}\otimes_{(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}}\kappa(\mathfrak q_K), $$
so the two conormal fibres have the same dimension. Its construction is the exactness of tensoring the sequence $I^2\subset I\subset P$ with the field $K$, followed by localization and residue-field base change; the hypotheses are precisely the presentation and prime contractions fixed in steps 1--2.

Assume $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$. The polynomial localization $P_{\mathfrak q'}\twoheadrightarrow C_{\mathfrak q}$ is a surjective local map from a regular local $k$-algebra, by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring]. The given complete-intersection presentation of $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is another surjective local map from a regular local $k$-algebra essentially of finite type, with kernel generated by a finite regular sequence in its maximal ideal. Hence [lem-trf-essentially-finite-type-ci-kernel-invariance] makes $IP_{\mathfrak q'}$ generated by a finite regular sequence. By [lem-weil-pbc-lci-regular-sequence-global-complete-intersection], there is $g\notin\mathfrak q$ for which $C_g$ is a global complete intersection over $k$.

source.place: Tag 00SI, proof lines 36249--36253, using the equivalent local criterion of Tag 00SC and then spreading the regular-sequence presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] to $C=P/I$, $\mathfrak q$ and the principal global-complete-intersection neighbourhood from step 4. It says $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$ is free of rank $n-d$. Therefore its residue-field fibre has dimension $n-d$. By steps 2--3, the $C_K$ conormal fibre at $\mathfrak q_K$ also has dimension $n-d$.

source.place: Tag 00SI, proof lines 36249--36256, comparing the common dimension and conormal generator number.

proof.text: The module $(I_K/I_K^2)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is finitely generated because $I_K$ is finitely generated in the Noetherian polynomial ring [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-field-regular-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Its fibre has dimension $n-d$, so [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] gives $n-d$ local generators. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-generators-global-complete-intersection] over $K$ produces $g_K\notin\mathfrak q_K$ with $(C_K)_{g_K}$ a global complete intersection. The pointwise criterion [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] then identifies the localization $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ with a complete-intersection local ring over $K$.

source.place: Tag 00SI, proof lines 36253--36259, Nakayama and the local criterion.

proof.text: Conversely assume $(C_K)_{\mathfrak q_K}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $K$. Repeating step 4 over $K$ (with $P_K,I_K,\mathfrak q_K$) gives a principal neighbourhood of $\mathfrak q_K$ on which $C_K$ is a global complete intersection. Step 5 over $K$ and [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-free-rank-codimension] therefore show that the $C_K$ conormal fibre has dimension $n-d$. By the comparison in step 3, the $C$ conormal fibre at $\mathfrak q$ has dimension $n-d$. Nakayama gives $n-d$ generators for $(I/I^2)_{\mathfrak q}$, and [lem-weil-pbc-lci-conormal-generators-global-complete-intersection] over $k$ gives $g\notin\mathfrak q$ with $C_g$ global complete intersection. The pointwise criterion [lem-trf-lci-pointwise-criterion] then gives that $C_{\mathfrak q}$ is a complete-intersection local ring over $k$.

source.place: Tag 00SI, proof lines 36249--36259, the converse with the two corresponding primes.
